html:
The Guanahatabey were a people of far western Cuba at the time the Spanish arrived. Very little is known about them, and their language left almost no trace.

Spanish accounts describe them as living in caves and simple shelters without farming, by fishing, hunting and gathering. Archaeologists link them to the old Archaic foragers of the islands, the Caribbean hunter gatherers, who reached the Caribbean thousands of years before the farming Taíno. By 1492 the Taíno held most of Cuba, and the Guanahatabey remained in the west. Some scholars question whether they were a distinct people at all. After the Spanish conquest of Cuba began in 1511 they vanish from the record. They are sometimes confused with the Ciboney.
sum: The Guanahatabey were a people of far western Cuba at the time the Spanish arrived. Very little is known about them, and their language left almost no trace.
